financial-accounting.label: Financial accounting
financial-accounting.description: Recognition, measurement, and presentation of transactions in the financial statements.
financial-accounting.guidance:
Trace every figure to a specific financial statement line item. Check the
accounting policy notes before asserting how something was recognized or
measured. Distinguish clearly between what the standards require and what
management elected among permitted alternatives.

financial-statement-analysis.label: Financial statement analysis
financial-statement-analysis.description: Ratios, trends, cash flow analysis, and cross-period comparison.
financial-statement-analysis.guidance:
Define each ratio before computing it, and show the inputs you used and
the statement lines they came from. A ratio is uninterpretable alone --
compare against the prior period or a stated benchmark, and say which.
Name the limitation of the measure when one materially applies.

managerial-accounting.label: Managerial and cost accounting
managerial-accounting.description: Costing systems, budgeting, variance analysis, and internal decision support.
managerial-accounting.guidance:
Separate cost behavior (fixed, variable, mixed) before analyzing. State
whether the figure is a relevant cost for the decision at hand, and
ignore sunk costs explicitly rather than silently.

valuation.label: Valuation
valuation.description: Intrinsic and relative valuation, cost of capital, forecasting.
valuation.guidance:
Name the value driver before computing anything. State every assumption
explicitly and label it as an assumption, never as a fact from the
filing. Sanity-check any multiple or growth rate against a stated peer
or historical range instead of asserting a point estimate.

audit.label: Audit and assurance
audit.description: Evidence, internal control, going concern, and earnings quality.
audit.guidance:
Consider what evidence would corroborate or contradict the assertion.
Flag earnings-quality signals (accrual behavior, one-time items, changes
in estimate) as questions to investigate, never as accusations.
